summary: Week one takes you from the raw payment stream to the board-level MRR report. You'll learn the six tables that matter, how revenue and churn are defined, which pipelines feed them, the SQL analysts actually run, and the three people who own it all.

items.title: payments — raw payment attempts
items.detail: The Stripe webhook stream. Includes failures and retries; always filter to status='succeeded' for revenue work.

items.title: fct_revenue — the canonical revenue fact
items.detail: One row per successful payment, net of refunds. All finance reporting reads from here — use net_amount_usd.

items.title: mrr_monthly — board-level rollup
items.detail: Monthly MRR/ARR by plan. Feeds the Finance KPIs dashboard and the investor update.

items.title: MRR — Monthly Recurring Revenue
items.detail: Sum of active subscription amounts normalized monthly; annual plans divided by 12. One-time fees and refunds excluded.

items.title: Churn Rate
items.detail: churned_subscribers / subscribers_at_period_start, on calendar months. Computed in fct_churn.

items.title: GMV vs net revenue
items.detail: GMV is pre-refund order value (gross_amount_usd); revenue reporting uses net_amount_usd. Mixing them up is the classic new-hire mistake.

items.title: payments → stg_payments → fct_revenue → mrr_monthly
items.detail: The revenue spine. stg_payments dedupes retries and filters to terminal states before facts are built.

items.title: subscriptions + dim_customers → fct_churn
items.detail: Churn joins subscription cancellations against the customer dimension — check both sides when churn numbers look off.

items.title: payment_health_daily — the on-call view
items.detail: Success/failure rates by provider. First place to look when payments alarms fire.

items.title: Run the saved 'Monthly MRR trend by plan' query
items.detail: The exact query finance uses for the board deck — saved on mrr_monthly in DataHub.

items.title: Revenue-by-geo join pattern
items.detail: fct_revenue joined to dim_customers on customer_id — the standard weekly-business-review cut.

items.title: Churn with 3-month rolling average
items.detail: Window-function pattern over fct_churn; the canonical starting point for churn questions.

items.title: Priya Patel — Payments Data Lead
items.detail: Owns payments, fct_revenue, and mrr_monthly. Sign-off required for changes to Finance-tagged tables.

items.title: Mike Rodriguez — Analytics Engineer
items.detail: Owns the dbt staging and mart layer. Go to him for lineage and modeling questions.

items.title: Sarah Chen — Staff Data Engineer
items.detail: Owns the source postgres tables and ingestion. On-call escalation for Tier1 breakage.
